newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian stocks mixed, further growth expected.
newsitem.headline: Croatian stocks mixed, further growth expected.

text.p: Croatian stocks closed mixed on Thursday, with mild gains in fully listed issues and further losses for hoteliers, but traders predicted Increased activity with further growth for most stocks.
"After Zagrebacka Banka broke the 1,000 kuna resistance, it is moving upward," said a trader with IFC brokerage.
He added that the same could be expected for drugs firm Pliva, though on smaller volumes.
Of nine active issues, five rose and four fell. Volume was lower at 8,811, turnover also down at 7.7 million kuna.
The biggest gainer Pliva, listed on the London Stock Exchange, edged up 99 kuna to 12,900, with 125 shares sold.

Zagrebacka, also fully listed, inched up five kuna to 1,030, but was the most actively traded issue with 2,726 units sold. The bank's E-series shares continued their recent growth, adding 10 kuna to 410, with 810 shares sold.
Brokers predicted brisker trade in Istrian hoteliers, following a recent correction, but said they would probably stagnate at current levels.
The only gainer among hotel stocks was Arenaturist, recovering five kuna to 250.
Istraturist was the biggest loser, down 11 kuna on volume of 200 shares. Laguna lost 10 kuna to 1,550, with 569 shares traded.

Confectioner Kras and food processor Podravka also recorded mild losses, edging down 10 and 7.10 kuna, respectively. But the two were among most active issues, with Kras selling 2,364 and Podravka 2,482 units.
Traders said both were likely to rise in the near future.
Brewery Karlovacka Pivovara was among Thursday's gainers, up 4 kuna to 200, with 50 shares changing hands.
The second tranche of public debt refinancing bonds edged up to 7.65 from 4.35 percent above par, on turnover of 7.7 million kuna.
The central bank exchange rate was set at 5.4861 kuna to the dollar, easing from Wednesday's 5.4684.
